eda01_sentences_by_split_source.caption: SkillSpan: sentences per split (train 4,800 / dev 3,174 / test 3,569), coloured by source (tech vs house).

eda01_tokens_per_sentence.caption: Tokens per sentence by source; 99% of sentences are shorter than the 128-token training limit.

eda01_span_length_hist.caption: Span length distribution (tokens): skill spans are multi-word verb phrases (median 4), knowledge spans are mostly 1–2 tokens.

eda01_top_skill_phrases.caption: The 30 most frequent skill phrases in the training split — dominated by soft skills ('communication skills', 'team player').

eda01_top_knowledge_phrases.caption: The 30 most frequent knowledge phrases in the training split — programming languages, frameworks and degrees.

eda01_pos_patterns.caption: Part-of-speech patterns of spans: skills are VERB+… phrases or NOUN+NOUN ('communication skills'); knowledge is PROPN/NOUN heads.

eda01_ngrams_tech_vs_house.caption: Top bigrams per source: tech postings are about software development, experience and flexible working; house postings mix application boilerplate ('further information', 'please contact') with business domains ('supply chain', 'project management').

eda01_entities.caption: spaCy entity labels in SkillSpan sentences: ORG/GPE are mostly scrubbed to placeholders; DATE and CARDINAL ('3+ years') dominate what remains.

eda01_tagged_example.caption: A SkillSpan sentence with its merged BIO tags (blue = skill, orange = knowledge).

eda02_label_status_by_subset.caption: Label status per benchmark subset: in TECH ads about 43% of annotated skill phrases cannot be mapped to ESCO (mostly LABEL NOT PRESENT) and 37% in HOUSE — the gap the 'not in ESCO' detector targets; TECHWOLF has sentence-level ESCO labels only.

eda02_top_esco_labels.caption: The most frequent ESCO target skills: a long tail — the top 25 skills cover only a small share of phrases, so retrieval must handle thousands of rare labels.

eda02_esco_label_length.caption: Token length of the ~13.9k ESCO skill labels: most are 2–5-word verb phrases ('manage musical staff'), which is why a bi-encoder (not keyword match) is needed.

eda02_sentence_length.caption: Sentence length per subset: TECH sentences are shortest (median ~10 tokens), HOUSE sentences the longest (median 15–18 tokens).

eda02_spans_per_sentence.caption: Number of annotated skill phrases per sentence: most sentences carry 1–3 phrases; a few list-style sentences carry 10+.

eda02_unmapped_terms.caption: Phrases annotators could not map to ESCO 1.1.0: concrete frameworks, tools and platforms (ReactJS, Docker, Django, Spring, Azure, Node.js…) — exactly the vocabulary a job-matching product must track outside the taxonomy.

p1_f1_comparison_test.caption: Problem 1: strict and loose span F1 per approach and span type on the SkillSpan test split (identical sentence set for all approaches; tagger = mean over seeds).

p1_false_positives_test.caption: Problem 1: over-extraction on sentences without any gold span (headers, benefits) — how often each approach invents a span where annotators found none.

p1_f1_by_source_test.caption: Problem 1: strict span F1 split by posting source (tech vs house) — the domain gap each approach suffers.

p2_workrb_map_val.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB MAP per task on the val split — lexical and dense baselines, the in-house fine-tuned MiniLM, the published ConTeXT encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM re-ranking (challenger).

p2_workrb_rp10_val.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB RP@10 per task on the val split — lexical and dense baselines, the in-house fine-tuned MiniLM, the published ConTeXT encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM re-ranking (challenger).

p2_workrb_mrr_val.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB MRR per task on the val split — lexical and dense baselines, the in-house fine-tuned MiniLM, the published ConTeXT encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM re-ranking (challenger).

p2_workrb_map_test.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB MAP per task on the test split — lexical and dense baselines, the in-house fine-tuned MiniLM, the published ConTeXT encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM re-ranking (challenger).

p2_workrb_rp10_test.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB RP@10 per task on the test split — lexical and dense baselines, the in-house fine-tuned MiniLM, the published ConTeXT encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM re-ranking (challenger).

p2_workrb_mrr_test.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB MRR per task on the test split — lexical and dense baselines, the in-house fine-tuned MiniLM, the published ConTeXT encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM re-ranking (challenger).

eda03_missing_values.caption: Djinni: share of missing/empty values per field for job postings and candidate profiles (CV free-text fields such as 'Looking For' and 'Highlights' are often empty).

eda04_postings_by_source.caption: Live snapshot: number of postings per applicant-tracking-system source (Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever, …).

eda04_salary_missingness.caption: Salary availability in the live snapshot: most postings leave compensation fields empty.

eda04_top_titles.caption: Most frequent job titles across the whole live snapshot.

eda04_departments.caption: Live snapshot sample: distribution of department.

eda04_employment_type.caption: Live snapshot sample: distribution of employment type.

eda04_description_length.caption: Length of live postings after HTML stripping (postings with text only): median 668 words — several times longer than a Djinni posting.

eda04_posting_dates.caption: Posting dates in the sample: the snapshot contains postings that are still open, so dates spread over several months with a recent peak.

eda04_ai_role_families.caption: The live demo index: data/AI/ML postings grouped into role families by title pattern.

eda04_description_coverage_by_source.caption: Only the Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Rippling and Gem feeds return posting bodies; Workday and SmartRecruiters listings are title-only, so the live index can only cover postings with text.

p2_nil_threshold_sweep_p2_biencoder.caption: Tuning the 'not in ESCO' cosine threshold on the TECH validation spans: joint accuracy, NIL-decision F1 and accuracy on mapped phrases vs threshold.

p2_nil_results_p2_biencoder.caption: 'Not in ESCO' detection on TECH and HOUSE test spans: joint accuracy, F1 of the NIL decision and accuracy on mapped phrases for the thresholded in-house fine-tuned MiniLM bi-encoder vs retrieve-then-LLM (challenger).

p2_nil_threshold_sweep.caption: Tuning the 'not in ESCO' cosine threshold on the TECH validation spans: joint accuracy, NIL-decision F1 and accuracy on mapped phrases vs threshold.

p2_nil_results.caption: 'Not in ESCO' detection on TECH and HOUSE test spans: joint accuracy, F1 of the NIL decision and accuracy on mapped phrases for the thresholded bi-encoder (champion) vs retrieve-then-LLM (challenger).

eda03_text_length.caption: Djinni text lengths: job postings are typically 150–400 words; CVs are much more variable, with a long tail of multi-page profiles and a spike of one-liners.

eda03_supply_demand.caption: Supply–demand by category: number of candidate profiles vs job postings for the 20 largest job categories on Djinni.

eda03_supply_demand_heatmap.caption: Supply–demand heatmap: relative job postings, candidate profiles and CVs-per-posting ratio per category — where competition for a job is highest.

eda03_experience_years.caption: Years of experience required by postings vs reported by candidates — postings cluster at 1–3 years, profiles have a longer tail.

eda03_english_level.caption: English level required by postings vs reported by candidates.

eda03_postings_per_month.caption: Monthly job postings per category on Djinni, 2020–2023: growth through 2021, a steady decline through 2022 and a partial recovery in 2023 (the last month of the dataset is incomplete).

eda03_wordclouds.caption: Word clouds of job postings for the six largest categories (800 postings each): the vocabulary differs sharply between stacks.

eda03_umap_market_map.caption: Market map: UMAP projection of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings for 5,000 job postings and 5,000 candidate profiles (10 largest categories) — categories form clear clusters, and profiles occupy the same regions as postings.

eda03_category_similarity.caption: Cosine similarity between category centroids of posting embeddings — used to define 'related' categories when sampling the labelled job pools.

eda03_entities.caption: spaCy entity labels in Djinni job descriptions: ORG (companies, frameworks mis-typed as organisations), GPE (locations) and DATE dominate.

p3_silver_eval.caption: Problem 3 silver set: ranking quality with 'same job category' as a rough relevance signal, over the whole 6k-posting index (baseline on all sampled CVs, agents on a subset).

eda05_synthetic_length.caption: TechWolf's synthetic ESCO sentences are uniformly short (one or two clauses), unlike real job-ad sentences — a domain gap for the bi-encoder.

eda05_synthetic_openings.caption: Template bias in the generated training sentences: a handful of openings ('experience in …', 'ability to …') dominate, which the NO_DUPLICATES batch sampler and real-sentence evaluation guard against.

eda05_llm_phrases_per_sentence.caption: Over-/under-generation of the few-shot LLM extractor: distribution of phrases per sentence compared with the gold annotation.

eda05_llm_phrase_length.caption: Length of LLM-returned phrases: skill phrases are long, knowledge phrases short — the same shape as the gold spans.

eda05_rtl_selected.caption: Retrieve-then-LLM: number of ESCO candidates the LLM accepts per sentence; zero means it judged none of the retrieved skills a true mention.

eda05_fit_by_relation.caption: Bias check: distribution of agent fit scores for same-, related- and random-category jobs — scores should fall across tiers; overlap shows where the agents are over-generous.

eda05_fit_by_label.caption: Calibration check: agent fit scores against the gold 0/1/2 labels.

eda05_unsupported_reasons.caption: Failure modes of generated explanations: reason codes of unsupported claims (quote not found in resume / job, skill not in the quotes, missing skill actually present).

eda05_rater_agreement.caption: Agreement between the two LLM raters on the 300 resume–job fit labels (confusion matrix; disagreements were adjudicated).

p3_ranking_quality_agent.caption: Problem 3: nDCG@10, Precision@3 and MRR (relevant = strong fit, and relevant = partial fit or better) of the embedding baseline, the single ReAct agent and the multi-agent pipeline on the same 30 labelled 10-job pools.

p3_hallucination_agent.caption: Problem 3: hallucination rate of the explanations (unsupported claims ÷ all claims, automatic checker) — the verifier's effect.

p3_efficiency_agent.caption: Problem 3: LLM calls, cost and latency per resume for each approach (same model and tools).
